meta.title: Point at the page and attach screenshots today

security.label: Step with an evidenced pain point

nodes.label: Chat, Alt or a tool
nodes.explanation: Three ways in. Chat in the toolbar opens the panel and, with it, the floating tools at the top of the page: Select Elements, Arrow, Line, Box and Undo Drawing. Holding Alt (Option on macOS) starts selection from anywhere, even while typing in the chat composer, but not in the page's own fields; the first marker opens chat by itself. The Alt listener checks only the key, not whether Ctrl, Shift or Meta is held too, so every chord that includes Alt, devhost's own Restart Changed shortcut Alt+Ctrl+R included, turns selection on until Alt is released: the outline and cursor flash over the page, and a click made meanwhile marks an element instead of reaching the page; on macOS so does every Option character typed in the composer, which on many European layouts includes @, brackets and braces (keyboard-and-screen-reader-07). The tools work over the page's own popovers and modal dialogs without closing them, and Escape leaves selection or drawing mode.

sources.label: Chat button in the toolbar
Hold Alt to start selecting
Floating Select, Arrow, Line, Box, Undo

nodes.label: Click elements to mark
nodes.explanation: In selection mode each click on a page element adds a numbered marker (#1, #2, ...) and a row in Page context; the first marker opens chat. Only a pointer can pick: no key moves the outline or marks an element (page-context-10). While any toolbar notice shows, such as the default hot reloading notice, the toolbar's container spans the bar's whole width and its empty part still takes pointer events, so elements just above the toolbar cannot be clicked or marked: the click lands on devhost's own surface, and nothing says why (page-context-03, owned by toolbar-shell). The hint reads 'Click Elements To Add Context. Esc To Finish.' beside an Esc key cap, naming Esc twice (page-context-08). Each pick returns focus to the chat composer, so while the agent's turn runs, Esc to finish can also stop that turn, depending on which of two Escape listeners registered last (keyboard-and-screen-reader-06). Releasing Alt or switching windows ends even a toggle-latched selection, so an Option character typed in the composer or Alt+Ctrl+R silently ends it and the next click acts on the page (page-context-11). A marker keeps its number only until an earlier one is removed (see Review Page context).

sources.label: Click adds marker #(count + 1)
Whole toolbar container takes pointer events
A devhost surface wins over the page

nodes.label: Draw Arrow, Line or Box
nodes.explanation: Choosing Arrow, Line or Box and dragging draws one shape, and the tool then switches itself off, so each further shape needs the tool again. Only a press-and-drag draws: no key places or sizes a shape, and a start click and an end click draw nothing (page-context-10). While a tool is armed the pointer hint reads 'Drag To Draw A arrow. Esc To Cancel.', with the lowercase tool ID and the wrong article, beside its own Esc key cap (page-context-08). Shapes are stored as document coordinates and follow only scrolling and window resizing: when the app's layout moves without a scroll (a validation message disappears, data arrives, the agent's own hot update lands) or a narrower window re-centers the page, a box or arrow stays behind and frames a different element, and the agent receives those stale coordinates (page-context-02). With no tool chosen a shape can be dragged by its stroke, and Undo Drawing always removes the newest shape: it never reverses a move and has no redo or keyboard shortcut (page-context-04).

sources.label: Points stored as document coordinates
Re-read only on resize and scroll
Undo Drawing drops the newest shape

nodes.label: Review Page context
nodes.explanation: Page context in the chat panel lists each marker as '#n label' and each drawing as 'n. kind' (1. box) by list position. Removing a marker renumbers every later one on the page and in the list, while the message already typed keeps its #numbers, which now point at different elements, with no warning and Send still enabled (page-context-01). Drawings carry no number on the page and hovering a row highlights nothing, so two boxes cannot be told apart, and Clear Page Context removes everything at once with no undo (page-context-04). Nothing here shows the element path, nearby text, styles or URL that will be sent (page-context-07).

sources.label: Rows: '#n label' and 'n. kind' only
Remove renumbers remaining markers
Clear Page Context, no undo

nodes.label: Share Tab in the picker
nodes.explanation: Share Tab, next to Send Message, opens the browser's own picker. Only a browser tab is accepted: choosing a window or screen stops the stream with 'Select this browser tab to include the page and its annotations.' Closing the picker on purpose, or any other refusal, puts the browser's raw rejection text in a red alert under Page context, announced as an alert, and it stays through later sends until the next Share Tab or a reload (page-context-09). While Include Tab Snapshot (the camera) is on, every message takes a fresh screenshot of the tab; the share lasts until Stop Sharing, a reload or the browser's own stop control, and devhost never sends video.

sources.label: Share Tab, camera toggle, Stop Sharing
Picker; windows and screens rejected
Any other refusal: raw browser text kept

nodes.label: Write and Send Message
nodes.explanation: The person refers to markers by number in the message ('make #1 match #2'), as the docs teach, and chooses Send Message. Chat stores the draft first, then prepares page context before delivering: the page title and URL, the markers, the drawings and, while a tab is shared and the camera is on, a screenshot. Without a shared tab the message goes to delivery with markers and drawings only. Page context controls stay disabled until the send settles.

sources.label: Draft saved; context prepared, then sent
beforeSend: title, URL, marks, capture

nodes.label: Capture tab, build markers
nodes.explanation: With a shared tab, devhost hides its own toolbar, chat and tooltips while keeping the markers and drawings, waits until a captured frame shows them gone, and takes one image; if it cannot confirm that, the send fails and keeps the draft. Then each marker's payload is built: element path, full path, CSS classes, nearby text, accessibility, bounds, computed styles in two formats, and the component's source location. On React 19 development builds that lookup finds nothing, because it reads only the source fields older React versions set, so markers reach the agent without a file and the agent searches the code for the component (page-context-06, owned by component-source).

sources.label: Hide devhost surfaces, wait for paint
Marker payload fields
Reads only pre-React-19 source fields

nodes.label: Crop the screenshot
nodes.explanation: Share Screenshot opens over the page with the captured frame: drag to select an area, or set Left, Top, Width and Height from the keyboard, then choose Share Selected Area or Share Whole Tab. It shows only the image: nothing here or earlier shows the element details, the full URL, the nearby text or the coordinates sent with it, and that text can carry customer data or tokens even when the crop shows none (page-context-07). Cancel or Escape cancels the send and keeps the draft and context.

sources.label: Crop preview: image and three buttons
JSON appended to the message text

nodes.label: Control server to agent
nodes.explanation: The browser sends the text, which now ends in 'Page context:' and one line of JSON, with the image as one command to the stack's control server. The server appends the devhost workflow instructions, refuses a message over 8 MiB or an image that is not PNG or JPEG, and queues the message for the conversation's agent; Codex receives the text and the image as one input. The agent gets the page title, the full URL, every marker field, the drawing coordinates, and the screenshot's size and crop.

sources.label: Send command with text and images
Workflow instructions; 8 MiB limit
Codex input: text and image

nodes.label: Read the sent message
nodes.explanation: Sending clears the markers and drawings that went out. The sent message shows the typed text; the page data sits behind a collapsed Page Context button as pretty-printed JSON in a 240 px scroll box, about 15 of 60 lines visible. Marker bounds and drawings are in page CSS pixels while the screenshot is a crop in captured-image pixels, and no viewport size, scroll offset or scale is sent, so neither the person nor the agent can place a marker or box on the screenshot, and a drawing names no element (page-context-07).

sources.label: Page Context split from the typed text
Collapsed raw JSON, 240 px box
Sent markers and drawings cleared

nodes.label: Reload drops page context
nodes.explanation: A reload (the browser's own, Reload on a Reload blocked notice, a worktree switch, or an agent edit that refreshes the page) restores chat, its side and the unsent draft exactly, but markers, drawings and the tab share live only in memory and are gone. Nothing says context was dropped: the draft still names #1 and #2, Send Message stays enabled, and sending gives the agent references to nothing (journey-agent-fix-04; page-context-05 is its duplicate, adding drawings and agent-triggered reloads). The docs say selections do not survive a reload; the interface never does.

sources.label: Persisted chat state: draft, no context
Shapes and markers in memory only
Docs: selections do not survive a reload

nodes.label: Send cancelled or failed
nodes.explanation: Cancel or Escape in the crop preview, a capture that cannot confirm devhost's surfaces are hidden, or a send the server rejects (such as one over 8 MiB) ends the send without delivering it. The panel shows why ('Screenshot sharing cancelled. Your draft and page context have been retained.'), and the draft, markers and drawings stay for another try, as the docs promise.

sources.label: Cancel: draft and context retained
Failed send: error shown, nothing cleared
Docs: a cancelled or failed send keeps them

cards.title: What already works
items: Three ways in: Chat, the floating tools, or holding Alt (Option), which also works while typing in the composer but not in the page's own fields
Markers and drawings work over the page's own popovers and modal dialogs without closing them, and Escape leaves either mode even from the composer
Tab sharing accepts only a browser tab; devhost hides its own toolbar, chat and tooltips in the image, or fails the send and keeps the draft
The crop preview offers Share Selected Area, Share Whole Tab and keyboard Left, Top, Width and Height fields; one image per message, never video
Sending clears only what was sent; a cancelled, failed or oversized send keeps the draft, markers and drawings
The sent message keeps the exact page data that went out behind its Page Context button

cards.title: Tickets on this journey
items: page-context-03 While a toolbar notice shows, an invisible strip above the toolbar swallows clicks, so elements there cannot be marked (owned by toolbar-shell)
page-context-06 On React 19 development builds markers reach the agent without a source location (owned by component-source)
page-context-01 Removing a marker renumbers the rest, so #numbers already typed point at other elements
page-context-02 Drawings keep fixed page coordinates when the layout moves, so they frame a different element
page-context-04 Undo Drawing removes the newest shape, not the last action; drawing rows cannot be matched to the page; Clear has no undo
page-context-07 Nothing before Send shows the page data that leaves; afterwards it is raw JSON whose coordinates do not match the screenshot
journey-agent-fix-04 A reload drops every marker and drawing without notice but restores the draft that refers to them
page-context-05 Duplicate of journey-agent-fix-04 (same reload step), adding drawings and agent-triggered reloads
keyboard-and-screen-reader-06 Pressing Esc to finish Select Elements, as its hint says, can also stop the agent's running turn, though not every time
page-context-08 The drawing hint reads 'Drag To Draw A arrow.', and both annotation hints spell out Esc beside their own Esc key cap
page-context-09 Cancelling the tab picker shows the browser's raw rejection as a red alert that stays until the next Share Tab
page-context-10 Marking and drawing need a pointer: keyboard users can turn the tools on but never pick or draw, and drawing has no two-click path
keyboard-and-screen-reader-07 Any chord that includes Alt, devhost's own Alt+Ctrl+R included, turns on Select Elements while it is held
page-context-11 Releasing Alt or switching windows ends a selection the toggle latched, so the next click acts on the page

cards.title: Evidence
items: Traced from alexgorbatchev/devhost at edb5c0fc01cabae490e92ac23d4c785ec896c4ed; the review exercised build 0.0.12 live: marking and removing markers, Arrow, Line and Box with a move and Undo Drawing, a layout change and a narrower window, Clear Page Context, a reload, Share Tab with the crop preview, Cancel and Share Selected Area, and one sent message with page context. The picker's refusal, Include Tab Snapshot off, Stop Sharing, a failed send, Alt chords, an Alt release or window switch during a toggled selection, and keyboard-only picking and drawing were read in code only. This diagram was traced from source only.
